note: AN ANCHOR WHERE IT CAN NEVER MATCH, and the one case in this group that AGREED BEFORE THE WORK -- (nil nil) on both sides -- which is why it carried `expect: agree' while the row was divergent, and keeps it now that the row is supported. It agrees for two different reasons, and that is the point: Emacs matches nothing because `\\`' can only match at offset 0 and there is an `a' before it, while kg matches nothing because it reads `\\`' as a literal backtick and the subject has none (phase26-anchor-literal-backtick-today measures that directly). After 26.2 taught the spellings the answer is still (nil nil), now for Emacs' reason on both sides -- an implementation that made a mid-pattern anchor match anything would have failed here.
